sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate preserves the prior repairs, uses only the canonical project namespace and supplied terms, targets ship-owned and directAnalysisCase-owned properties correctly, enforces the required quantity datatypes and units, represents the vertical and horizontal alternatives on each case, requires the several-case vertical coverage and centered horizontal case, and preserves the conditional loadPatchLength/iceLoadAreaFactorCa pairing within the COMPLEX_READINESS boundary. Deterministic validation is valid; no matcher activation is needed.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Add the declared position semantics to each directAnalysisCase. Numeric verticalLoadPosition and horizontalLoadPosition alone do not encode the required UIWL-centered, 0.5h0-below-LIWL, intermediate-vertical, mid-span/-spacing-centered, and other horizontal checks. Require the canonical verticalLoadPositionType and horizontalLoadPositionType relationships with the appropriate controlled values, and include the required UIWL/LIWL reference positions and ship spacing/span inputs where needed to establish those positions. Preserve the existing conditional loadPatchLength/iceLoadAreaFactorCa pairing and complex-readiness boundary.

Repair the position alternative shapes so they constrain each directAnalysisCase, not the loadPositionTypeValue node reached by sh:node. The vertical alternatives must test the case's verticalLoadPositionType for upperIceWaterlineCenteredPosition, halfLoadHeightBelowLowerIceWaterlinePosition, or intermediateVerticalPosition, with the required upper/lower reference positions on that same case; the current first branch incorrectly tests horizontalLoadPositionType. Likewise constrain horizontalLoadPositionType alternatives directly on each case. Preserve the required position quantities, ship spacing/span inputs, conditional loadPatchLength and iceLoadAreaFactorCa pairing, and the COMPLEX_READINESS boundary from the prior instruction.

Repair the case-collection semantics while preserving both prior instructions and the COMPLEX_READINESS boundary. The current per-case sh:or only permits one of the vertical alternatives and one horizontal alternative, so a graph containing only repeated upper-UIWL or “other horizontal” cases can pass without requiring the mandated UIWL-centered case, 0.5h0-below-LIWL case, several intermediate vertical cases, or a mid-span/-spacing-centered case. Add collection-level qualified constraints on ship/nltl:hasDirectAnalysisCase for the required vertical controlled values and at least one centered horizontal case, with cardinalities reflecting the several-case requirement; retain the conditional several-case requirement when load length is not arrangement-determined. Also constrain the intermediateVerticalPosition branch’s upperIceWaterlineReferencePosition and lowerIceWaterlineReferencePosition as QuantityValue nodes with xsd:decimal numericValue and the canonical metre unit, rather than presence-only properties. Keep all case-owned position, combined bending/shear, capacity-minimizing, and conditional loadPatchLength/iceLoadAreaFactorCa requirements unchanged.

The candidate preserves the prior repairs, uses only the canonical project namespace and supplied terms, targets ship-owned and directAnalysisCase-owned properties correctly, enforces the required quantity datatypes and units, represents the vertical and horizontal alternatives on each case, requires the several-case vertical coverage and centered horizontal case, and preserves the conditional loadPatchLength/iceLoadAreaFactorCa pairing within the COMPLEX_READINESS boundary. Deterministic validation is valid; no matcher activation is needed.
